questions.title: Why does GRPO’s token‑level importance weight violate the principle of importance sampling?
questions.question_body: In Section 3 the authors claim that GRPO applies the importance weight \(w_{i,t}(\theta) = \frac{\pi_{\theta}(y_{i,t}\mid x, y_{i,<t})}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(y_{i,t}\mid x, y_{i,<t})}\) at each token position, which leads to high‑variance updates. I thought that importance sampling only requires the ratio of *full* target and behavior distributions, not per‑sample ratios. Could someone explain concretely why using a single‑sample ratio at each token breaks the unbiasedness property of importance sampling?

questions.title: What is the intuition behind taking the \(1/|y_i|\) power of the sequence likelihood ratio in GSPO?
questions.question_body:
GSPO defines the sequence‑level importance ratio as
\[
 s_i(\theta) = \left( \frac{\pi_{\theta}(y_i\mid x)}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(y_i\mid x)} \right)^{1/|y_i|}
 = \exp \left( \frac{1}{|y_i|}\sum_{t=1}^{|y_i|}\log \frac{\pi_{\theta}(y_{i,t}\mid x, y_{i,<t})}{\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(y_{i,t}\mid x, y_{i,<t})} \right).
\]
Why do the authors raise the ratio to the power \(1/|y_i|\)? Is this simply a length‑normalization to keep the scale comparable across different response lengths, or does it have a deeper statistical meaning (e.g., geometric mean)?

questions.title: How are the clipping ranges for GSPO (≈3e‑4) and GRPO (≈0.2) chosen, and why do they differ by orders of magnitude?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions that clipping ranges are set to 3e‑4 – 4e‑4 for GSPO and 0.2 – 0.27 for GRPO. Since both algorithms use a min‑clip formulation, I would expect similar ranges after normalizing importance weights. Is the difference purely due to the definition of \(s_i(\theta)\) versus \(w_{i,t}(\theta)\), or is there a principled way to tune these hyperparameters? What would happen if we used comparable ranges across both methods?

questions.title: What happens when the standard deviation of rewards in a group is zero?
questions.question_body:
Both GRPO and GSPO compute advantages as
\[
 \widehat{A}_i = \frac{r(x,y_i) - \operatorname{mean}\{r(x,y_j)\}_{j=1}^G}{\operatorname{std}\{r(x,y_j)\}_{j=1}^G}.
\]
If all sampled responses receive exactly the same reward, the denominator becomes zero. How do the authors handle this edge case? Does it cause numerical instability or affect gradient estimates?

questions.title: Why does clipping a larger fraction of tokens in GSPO still lead to higher training efficiency compared to GRPO?
questions.question_body: Figure 3 shows that GSPO clips two orders of magnitude more tokens than GRPO, yet achieves better sample efficiency. Intuitively I would think discarding more data hurts learning speed. Could someone explain why sequence‑level clipping removes noisy gradients more effectively than token‑level clipping, perhaps with reference to variance reduction arguments?

questions.title: How does GSPO‑token retain numerical equivalence with GSPO when all token advantages are identical?
questions.question_body: The authors state that GSPO‑token is numerically identical to GSPO when \(\widehat{A}_{i,t}=\widehat{A}_i\). They achieve this by detaching (sg) parts of the ratio. Could someone walk through a concrete example showing how the detach operation makes \(s_{i,t}(\theta) = s_i(\theta)\) and why gradients end up identical under this condition?

questions.title: What is ‘expert‑activation volatility’ in MoE models and why does it break GRPO’s token‑level importance ratios?
questions.question_body: Section 5.3 describes that after each RL update about 10 % of experts activated for a token change, which leads to drastic fluctuations in \(w_{i,t}(\theta)\. How exactly does this volatility propagate into unstable importance weights? Is there a formal relationship between routing changes and likelihood ratios that explains why sequence‑level ratios remain stable?

questions.title: Can you clarify how ‘Routing Replay’ works and why it is unnecessary under GSPO?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions caching expert routing decisions from the old policy and replaying them when computing token‑level ratios for GRPO. How is this implemented in practice (e.g., storing routing masks per token)? Moreover, why does switching from token‑level ratios to sequence‑level ratios eliminate the need for such caching?

questions.title: How does mini‑batch partitioning introduce an off‑policy setting, and how does sequence‑level clipping mitigate its effects?
questions.question_body: During RL training, rollout batches are split into multiple mini‑batches for gradient updates. This means samples are used after several parameter updates have already occurred, making them off‑policy. In PPO/GRPO this is handled by clipping per token. In GSPO we clip per response via \(s_i(\theta)\. How does this clipping bound the bias introduced by using stale samples across mini‑batches?

questions.title: Is there any theoretical guarantee that GSPO’s gradient estimator remains unbiased under certain conditions?
questions.question_body: "Gradient Analysis" derives an expression for \(∇_θ J_{GSPO}\). Does this estimator correspond to an unbiased estimate of \(∇_θ E_{π_θ}[r]\) when using clipped importance weights? If so, under what assumptions (e.g., small clipping range, large group size) does unbiasedness hold?

questions.title: Why does length normalisation in \(s_i(θ)\) reduce variance compared to using raw sequence likelihood ratios?
questions.question_body: If we omitted the exponent \(1/|y_i|\), we would have raw ratios that can vary dramatically with response length. How exactly does taking the geometric mean (or log‑average) lower variance? Is there an analytic argument based on properties of log‑normals or central limit theorem?

questions.title: (Advanced) How would GSPO be adapted for tasks where rewards are defined per turn rather than per full response?
questions.question_body: "GSPO-token" allows tokenwise advantage customization, but what about multi‑turn dialogues where each turn has its own reward signal? Could we define a turn‑level importance ratio analogous to sequences within a response? What modifications would be needed in the clipping and advantage computation steps?
